# Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity

**Company:** Corvale Mobility (fictional name; intercity rail and coach operator)
**Location:** Kraków, Poland (contract, remote-friendly; occasional office days)
**Engagement:** Service agreement (B2B / freelance), not an employment contract
**Rate:** 95 – 125 PLN per hour

## The engagement

Corvale is preparing a new generation of trains and needs a cloud infrastructure engineer for the team that links the vehicles to the company's cloud platform. You will help shape the architecture from the start and take it to production.

## Scope

- Design, build and operate the cloud infrastructure that links on-board train systems with backend services: telemetry ingestion, alerting, video streaming and remote content updates
- Maintain the infrastructure-as-code repository (Terraform with Terragrunt), keeping it tidy and approachable
- Lead technical proposals across backend and infrastructure from idea to production
- Contribute to system design and challenge decisions with arguments
- Set up secure train-to-cloud communication (mutual TLS, certificate management, network design)
- Agree interfaces and responsibilities with train manufacturers' engineers
- Support backend developers in deploying services that are easy to monitor and run
- Keep the platform observable, reliable and secure

## Requirements

- Hands-on infrastructure engineering and cloud environment design and operation
- AWS preferred; other major clouds acceptable
- Strong Terraform and Terragrunt
- Good understanding of systems architecture and system design
- Networking knowledge, including mTLS and SSL/TLS
- Practical security awareness
- Experience leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along
- Strong analytical thinking and clear communication

**Nice to have:** IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, backend or full-stack background (JVM preferred), Linux and virtual machines.

## Working model

Independent contractor, invoicing monthly for agreed services.

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role. In my current role at Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines and merge-request environments used by three product teams, supporting the delivery and testing of services through reliable, repeatable infrastructure workflows. I’m looking to build on this experience in a platform and infrastructure engineering role, and Corvale’s work connecting a new train fleet with cloud services makes this opportunity particularly compelling.

I’ve improved CI pipelines across three teams, reducing average run time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly runner costs by about 30%. I designed and delivered short-lived application and PostgreSQL environments for each merge request, with seeded data, Helm-based deployment to a shared Kubernetes cluster, end-to-end test execution and automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity. These projects required profiling systems, proposing and coordinating changes across three product teams, and bringing developers and QA stakeholders along through clearer CI documentation and visibility into flaky tests. I wrote Odrava’s internal guide to how CI works, which is used in onboarding, and mentored two QA interns.

My hands-on infrastructure engineering experience includes Linux, GitLab CI, Docker, Helm-based Kubernetes deployments, namespace-level operation of shared environments, and infrastructure-as-code practice with Terraform. Outside work, I built a three-node k3s homelab with GitOps deployments, monitoring, ingress and TLS certificate management, and provisioned a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform. I have also used AWS EC2 and S3 at a fundamentals level through personal free-tier projects. This has given me a practical foundation in infrastructure-as-code, automation, observability and test infrastructure, while my Terraform experience to date has been through personal projects.

Corvale’s engineering-led approach and emphasis on teams owning systems and solving problems collaboratively resonate with how I’ve approached improving shared CI and test environments. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could support the Fleet Connectivity team as it shapes reliable, observable infrastructure for the new fleet.

Thank you for your consideration.

Marta Kowal-Brandt
